newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran says foreign debt $20.4 bln in September 96.
newsitem.headline: Iran says foreign debt $20.4 bln in September 96.

text.p: Iran's foreign debt stood at about $20.4 billion in September, showing a decline of nearly $1.6 billion in the six months since March, the daily Iran said on Thursday.
Quoting Central Bank figures, it said the debt amounted to $20.369 billion on September 20, down $1.559 billion since the beginning of the current Iranian year on March 20, 1996.
Short-term debts accounted for $5.679 billion of the total debt amount and medium and long-term debts made up the balance, the newspaper said.
Iran also faced other external obligations of $13.331 billion, which included letters of credit for goods and services not yet received and future interest, it added.
It said Tehran was due to repay $5.239 billion in the next Iranian year (1997/98) which starts on March 21, 1997.

Iran would repay $7.154 billion in 1998/99, about $4.199 billion in 1999/2000, $2.628 billion in 2000/01, $637 million in 2001/02, $237 million in 2002/03 and $275 million from 2003/04, the newspaper said.
